lines.japanese:
……何がまずいって、とにかく翡翠がまずかった。
　琥珀さんと秋葉は不心得にも酒に慣れているらしかったが、翡翠にとってまともに飲むのは今日が初めてだという。
　だっていうのに俺に合わせての事なのか、頬を赤らめて一生懸命にグラスを口をつけて、その結果がコレだった。
lines.label: s323
lines.maoEnglish:
The greatest problem by far is Hisui.
Kohaku and Akiha appear to be disgracefully familiar with alcohol, but today was Hisui’s first time truly drinking.
Even so—perhaps because I was drinking—she kept gamely raising the glass to her lips with her cheeks flushed red, and this is the result.

lines.label: s323
lines.maoEnglish:
“Hisui? You don’t have to force yourself if it’s unpleasant.”
“……”
Hisui nods once.
Then she puts the glass to her lips again and lets her unfocused gaze drift into space.
No matter how often I try to stop her, she keeps taking tiny sips.
I don’t understand it, but perhaps she has discovered that she likes alcohol.

Whatever else may be said, she is magnificently drunk herself.

Ordinarily that would be harmless enough, but alcohol has rendered everything incomprehensible to her, transforming her into a machine that does nothing but mutter grievances.

lines.maoEnglish:
“I’m terribly sorry: I was so intoxicated that I lost track of everything. I seem to have decided that, with a bed directly in front of me, there was no need to return to my own room—”
Hisui explains, plainly mortified.
“R-right—of course that’s the sort of thing people do when they’re drunk.”
I let out an awkward little laugh.
Hisui draws her shoulders in with embarrassment.
Why is this so awkward?
All we did was sleep beside each other, yet now I’m painfully conscious of her and can’t think of a single thing to say.

“Exactly. So at least let me apologize without arguing. If you won’t, I’ll never be able to ask anything of you again.”

lines.japanese:
居間に行くと、すでに翡翠の姿があった。
　秋葉はすでに朝食を済ませて紅茶を飲んでいるし、琥珀さんは台所にいるらしい。
「おはよう兄さん。
今朝はいくらか早いんですね」
「ん？
　ああ、今朝はちょっとしたトラブル……」
　言いかけて、ちらりと翡翠の顔を盗み見る。
「いや、まあ鬼の霍乱ってヤツで早起きしただけ。
そういう秋葉もすごいじゃないか。
昨日あれだけ酔ってたのに、こんなに早く起きてくるなんて」
lines.label: s323

When I reach the sitting room, Hisui is already there.
Akiha has finished breakfast and is drinking tea, while Kohaku appears to be in the kitchen.
“Good morning, Brother. You’re rather early today.”
“Hm? Oh, there was a little trouble this morning…” I stop and steal a glance at Hisui.
“No, nothing—I wake up early once in a blue moon. You’re the impressive one, Akiha. After getting that drunk last night, I can’t believe you’re up already.”

lines.maoEnglish:
“It’s nothing complicated. Apparently, once alcohol enters the body, it turns into some highly toxic substance called aceto-something.
Since that would be bad, the liver produces enzymes that break the poison down and eventually turn the alcohol into plain water.
Different ethnic groups supposedly produce different amounts, and Japanese people tend to have relatively little. People who don’t produce much are what you’d call lightweights.”
Akiha’s eyes widen with interest.

「いや、べつに。

「ふうん。
そのわりには昨夜はあまりお飲みになられていなかったようですけど？」
「だから、俺はその下戸ってヤツなんだってば。
酒は気合で呑むものだー、なんていう悪友をね、論理的に改心させるにはこうゆうふうに苦労しないといけなくてさ」
　ちなみに、その悪友とは乾有彦に他ならない。
lines.label: s323
lines.maoEnglish:
“I’m astonished. How did you learn all that, Brother?”
“It’s nothing. I just happen to have a friend who’s a particularly obnoxious drunk.”
“Is that so? Yet you hardly seemed to drink anything last night.”
“That’s because I’m one of those lightweights. When your idiot friend insists that drinking is all about willpower, this is the kind of research it takes to argue him out of it.”
The idiot friend in question is, of course, Arihiko Inui.

“Certainly—I will fetch your schoolbag.”
Hisui hurries away toward the entrance hall, her footsteps pattering over the floor.
“…………”
I find myself staring dreamily after her.

lines.maoEnglish:
“Akiha, one question. Are you drunk?”
“Of course not. I’m not drunk at all. Akiha is going to stay perfectly sober until you’re completely plastered, Brother!”

lines.maoEnglish:
“Good grief. You were chirping all sorts of objections a moment ago, but it seems you do like alcohol after all, Brother.”
“Hey—what’s that supposed to mean? I’m not some great lover of drink.”
“Of course you are. You looked as though you were enjoying it immensely, so please spare me the excuses.”
Akiha leans across the table and picks up a bottle.
“I’ll dilute it with hot water—do you have any other requests?”
Without waiting for an answer, Akiha begins pouring whisky into my glass.
Common sense says I ought to stop her.
But she looks absurdly pleased with herself, so perhaps this is the moment to cast common sense and morality aside.

“Sometimes I wonder whether you are utterly indifferent—and whether, underneath it all, you are terribly lonely. I―――I know it is a foolish thought, but I can’t help having it.
No one can come first in your heart. Perhaps you lost the person who once did, a very long time ago.
When I was little, I thought it was enough if you cared for me at all. Since there was no one you could place first, I told myself that was enough.
But now, I――――”

lines.japanese:
「だめですよ秋葉さま。
秋葉さまみたいなザルと志貴さんを一緒にしないでください。
　ほら、志貴さんもはっきりお断りしないと大変ですよ。
秋葉さまはいくら飲んでも酔われないんですから、とことんまで付き合ったら夜が明けてしまいます」
「ちょっと琥珀！
　ザルってなによ、ザルって。
せめて酒仙とか酒豪とか、そういう言い方をしてくれない！？」
　むっ、と怒って、秋葉はぐいっと酒を飲んだ。
lines.label: s324
lines.maoEnglish:
“You mustn’t do that, Miss Akiha. You can’t compare Shiki with a bottomless drinker like yourself, Miss Akiha.
And Shiki, you had better refuse her properly or you’ll be in terrible trouble. No amount of alcohol can make Miss Akiha drunk, so if you stay with her to the bitter end, dawn will find you still drinking.”
“Kohaku! What do you mean, ‘bottomless’? At least call me a legendary drinker or a champion!”
Scowling indignantly, Akiha tosses back another glass.

lines.japanese:
時間が経過する。
　いつのまにか翡翠も目を覚ましていて、とりとめのない会話が流れた。
　アルコールのせいか会話の内容はよく覚えていない。
　ただ何の意味もない、温かい会話だった。
　そういったものに慣れていない自分は、柔らかい真綿に締められているような、不安定な居心地を味わっている。
　そのせいだろう。
　この時間がもう少し続いてくれればいいと思う反面、少し一人になりたい、と思ってしまった。
lines.label: s324
lines.maoEnglish:
Time passes.
At some point Hisui wakes, and we drift into idle conversation.
Perhaps because of the alcohol, I remember little of what we say.
It is warm and utterly meaningless.
Unaccustomed to such warmth, I feel as though soft silk were slowly tightening around me—a precarious, uneasy comfort.
Perhaps that is why.
Part of me wishes the evening would last a little longer, while another part longs to be alone.

lines.mirrorMoon:
It has gotten pretty late.
Hisui woke up eventually and we talked about unimportant things.
It's probably the fault of the alcohol, but I don't remember what we talked about at all.
Just meaningless, warm conversation.
Because I wasn't used to that kind of stuff, I settled into an insecure comfort, like hanging from a silken thread.
It's probably because of that.
On one hand, I thought it would be nice for this to continue, but on the other hand, I wanted a little time to myself.

“No, nothing like that. I only felt frightened all of a sudden. Listen, Brother. You aren’t going away again, are you?”

That also means that, one day, I will leave.

Colorless, exhausted air.

ただ自分は有間の家で誰にも迷惑をかけないいい子でいたから、今日のように気がねなく楽しむ事はなかっただけ。
lines.label: s324
lines.maoEnglish:
“Thank you, Kohaku. I had a wonderful time tonight.”
Still seated, I tell her from the bottom of my heart.
“What brought this on? Tonight was hardly anything worth thanking me for.”
“Maybe not, but I really did enjoy it. Thinking about it, this was the first time I’d ever let loose with my family. I suppose I’d always wanted something like this.”
It is not as though the Arima family never held gatherings like this. I simply spent my time there being the good boy who never inconvenienced anyone, so I never relaxed and enjoyed myself as freely as I did tonight.

「でも志貴さん。
貴方はこの屋敷にいるかぎり、志貴さんが憧れているような家族というものは手に入りませんよ。
　遠野家の親戚の方々はみな志貴さまを疎んじておられます。
志貴さんの味方は秋葉さまだけです。
　ですから、これからの生活は志貴さんにとって心苦しいものになるでしょう」
　……琥珀さんの言う事はもっともだ。
　八年前、俺は親父や親戚会議で勘当寸前にまで扱われたわけだから、そんな自分の立場が今になって良くなるとは思っていない。

lines.maoEnglish:

Life here will therefore become very painful for you.”
Kohaku is right.
Eight years ago, my father and the family council came close to disowning me, so I have no reason to think their opinion will have improved since then.

琥珀さんは言いにくい事を聞いてくる」
「はい、申し訳ありません。
わたしも酔ってしまっているみたいですね。
こんな事を尋ねるなんて、どうかしています」
　琥珀さんは笑顔だった。
　……なんだかそんな顔をされると、さっきの質問がまるで嘘だったかのように思える。
lines.label: s324
lines.maoEnglish:
“That’s cruel, Kohaku. You ask such difficult questions.”
“Yes, I’m sorry. It seems I may be drunk as well. I must be out of my mind to ask such things.”
Kohaku is smiling.
Her smile makes the question she just asked feel like a lie.

lines.mirrorMoon:

Saying such things, there must be something wrong with me."

…… Smiling like that, it makes it seem like she didn't even ask me something so serious.

lines.japanese:
「……琥珀さん。
さっきの話だけど。
やっぱりさ、自分の家に戻ってくるのは当たり前の事じゃないか。
秋葉を一人きりにしておけないし、有間の人たちに迷惑もかけられないだろ」
「では、それが志貴さんが戻られた理由なんですね」
　なるほど、と納得してくれる琥珀さん。
―――けど、それは嘘だ。
　本当はもう一つ―――秋葉の事より大切な出来事が、確かにあった。
lines.label: s324
lines.maoEnglish:
“Kohaku. About what you asked… It’s only natural to return to your own home. I couldn’t leave Akiha all alone, and I couldn’t keep burdening the Arimas.”
“Then that is why you came back, Shiki.”
Kohaku nods, apparently satisfied.
―――But it is a lie.
There was one other reason―――an event that mattered even more to me than Akiha.

「志貴さん？
　どうしたんですか？」
「……いや、違うんだ琥珀さん。
ホントはね、もう一つだけ大事な理由がある」
「へえ、それってもしかして秘密なコトなんですか？」
「……どうだろう。
秘密っていうわけじゃないけど、人には話したくない大事な思い出。
　俺はね、ここを出るときに借り物をしちゃたんだ。
それをきちんと返したくて、ここに帰ってきたんだよ」
「――――――――――」
　……それも、翡翠は覚えていなかった事だけど。
lines.label: s324
lines.maoEnglish:
“Shiki? What is it?”
“No, that wasn’t the whole truth. There’s one more important reason.”
“Oh—is it a secret?”
“I’m not sure. It isn’t exactly secret, but it’s a precious memory I don’t like sharing.
When I left this place, I borrowed something. I came home because I wanted to return it properly.”
“――――――――――”
Though Hisui herself did not remember any of it.

「酔いも冷めたし、部屋に戻ります。
それじゃ、また明日」
　片手をあげて中庭から立ち去る。
　琥珀さんは呆然と、そんな俺をいつまでも見送っていた。

lines.maoEnglish:
I rise from the chair.
“I’ve sobered up, so I’m going back to my room. See you tomorrow.”
With one hand raised in farewell, I leave the courtyard.
Kohaku remains there, stunned, watching me until I disappear.

lines.japanese:
――――二度とこの屋敷に入る事はできない。
　そう父親に断言されて部屋を出た時の気持ちを、今でもまだ覚えている。
　事故にあって、ずっと一人きりで、先生に出会った後、結局は一人に戻ったのだと知った時。
　俺は先生との約束を守れないで、無感動な人間になっていたと思う。
　その時、ただ一度だけ話しかけてきてくれた少女。
　……それが、唯一つの救いだった。
　あの言葉にどんな魔法がかかっていたのかは知らない。
lines.label: s324
lines.maoEnglish:
――――I would never be allowed inside this mansion again.
Even now, I remember how I felt when my father declared that and sent me from the room.
After the accident, after being alone for so long, after meeting my teacher only to discover that in the end I had been left alone once more.
I think I had become numb, unable to keep my promise to her.
Then a girl spoke to me, just once.
That alone saved me.
I do not know what magic those words possessed.
lines.mao_english:

I think I had become numb, unable to keep my promise to her.

I do not know what magic those words possessed.
lines.mirrorMoon:
----You can never come back to this mansion ever again.
I still remember the time when my father said those words to me, and my feelings as I left my room.
That time when I realized that I would be all alone, just like I was before I met Sensei.
Not being able to keep my promise with Sensei, I guess I became empty inside.
That time, the girl I spoke with only once.
…… that was my only saving grace.
I don't know what kind of magic was in those words.

But to the child I was then, those words mattered.
I have simply―――treasured them ever since.

「……仕方ないよな。
子供のころの約束なんだし」
　それは本当に仕方のない事だと思う。
　八年間は長い。
　それが子供の頃の約束だとしたら、覚えているほうがおかしいんだ。
「……寝るか」
　はあ、と深呼吸をして瞼を閉じる。
――――後には、深い水底に沈むような眠りがあった。

lines.maoEnglish:
“It can’t be helped. It was a promise between children.”
I truly believe that.
Eight years is a long time.
For a promise made in childhood, remembering would be stranger than forgetting.
“Time to sleep.”
I draw a deep breath and close my eyes.
――――Then sleep takes me, like sinking to the bottom of deep water.

――――Impossible.
I lunge without warning, and the figure meets me head-on.
My enemy’s weapon is another knife.
We each aim a killing stroke at the other’s throat, and the two attacks cancel each other perfectly.

減量の果てにリングにあがったボクサーが、生涯最高の敵と対峙した時のような、悦びに満ちた笑いだ。

The man laughs.
There is no mockery in the smile. It is pure delight, like a boxer who has starved himself down to weight and entered the ring to find the finest opponent of his life.
Most likely.
I am wearing the same smile.

“Always wanted to try one of these.”
Delighted, the man buys two cans of coffee.
“Heads up.”
“Right.”
I catch the coffee and the change.
The man sits beside me and takes a sip from his can.
Today has been nothing but this sort of thing.

“They’re training their endurance. Adulthood is difficult in all sorts of ways.”
“Oh, I get it. You’re smart.”
The man cackles happily.
I take a drink as well.
I agree completely. Anyone willing to consume something this poisonous must harbor a considerable death wish.

The most meaningless subject of all is our respective abilities.
My eyes, which can see the death of things,
and his body, which is exceedingly difficult to kill.
As we compare their workings—
“Wait. Does that mean you could kill the five senses?”
It makes no sense at all.

lines.maoEnglish:
“I see. So we’re out of step.”
“Right. Which side is abnormal doesn’t matter. The side standing outside society is the one that’s out of step.”
“Is that so? Perhaps society is the abnormal one.”
“Oh—what do you mean by that?”
“Exactly what I said. You mentioned it yourself.
It’s like a majority vote. The minority who disagree with everyone else are discarded as ‘useless.’
It doesn’t matter which side is right. Anyone who fails to fit with the majority gets shut out, right or wrong. There can be no universal standard for being out of step.”

What do you think of that?”
“Huh. People like that exist? Go on.”

そりゃあ事故で死んでしまう場合もある。

lines.maoEnglish:
“That’s all.
They fight, but they aren’t supposed to finish the other person off. Accidents happen, of course, and sometimes somebody dies. Yet when that happens, it generally isn’t treated as murder. Isn’t that incredible?”
“―――You mean they’re allowed to kill?”
“No, no. They aren’t allowed to kill. But they are allowed to kill. Quite a contradiction, isn’t it? And there’s more. Apparently a boxer’s fists can be treated as deadly weapons, so boxers aren’t supposed to get into street fights.”

lines.maoEnglish:

The world is the thing that has strayed from common sense.”

lines.maoEnglish:
Not that I bear any hostility toward boxing.
Of all the professions in the world, few demand such complete self-denial in pursuit of a single goal.
A boxer rejects every temptation and forges his own body.
Human beings are fascinated by strength they can readily understand. That is why contests will never disappear.
Among all competitors, those who choose a sport built on hurting others are possessed by something special.

lines.japanese:
何か、自己さえ忘れて打ち込める嗜好。
　それはその個人の自由にはならない。
　学問を崇拝する者、芸術に焼身する者、商業に邁進する者。
　それを個人で決定できるのなら、この世界はもう少し解りやすい、キレイなパズルになっているだろう。
　だがこのパズルは穴だらけだ。
　所々欠けているし、中にはまったく規格の異なるピースが混ざっている。
lines.label: s324
lines.maoEnglish:
A calling one can throw oneself into so completely that everything else disappears.
That is not something a person is free to choose.
Some worship scholarship, some immolate themselves for art, and some throw themselves into commerce.
If each person could choose that calling, the world would make a cleaner, more comprehensible puzzle.
But this puzzle is riddled with holes.
Pieces are missing everywhere, while others belong to a wholly different design.

lines.japanese:
「ふうん。
オマエ、よくしゃべるヤツだな。
昔さ、オマエみたいな友人がオレにもいたんだぜ。
　そいつはなんていうか……そうだな、何も持っていなかったんだ。
だから何も求めていなかったように見えたんだろう。
　それはなんていうか、ひどく孤高でさ。
孤高っていうのは孤独の別名だろ。
だからオレは、それが気になって仕方がなかった」
「……ふうん。
何も求めていない、か。
アンタはどうなんだ？
　何か欲しいものはある？」
「……どうだろう。
あった気がするが、思い出せない。
そういうオマエはどうだ？」
lines.label: s324
lines.maoEnglish:
“Huh. You talk a lot. I had a friend like you once.
How can I put it? He had nothing, so perhaps that was why he seemed to want nothing.
There was something fiercely aloof about him. But aloofness is only another word for loneliness, isn’t it? I could never stop thinking about him.”
“I see. Wanting nothing. What about you? Is there anything you want?”
“I don’t know. Feels like there was, but I can’t remember. How about you?”

lines.japanese:
「求めているものは誰にだってあるだろ。
けど夢中になれるような事はなかった。
　自己を見失うほどの白熱は、そうだな―――今夜のこれが初めてだったかもしれない」
「あはは。
つまるところおまえも殺人鬼って事だよな、それは」
「……どうだろう。
まだ断定はできない。
そういうアンタはどうなんだ？
　人殺しは楽しいかい？」
「――――バカかオマエ。
楽しかったら休むことなくやってるだろ。
こんなのにはさ、理由はねえんだよ。
ただやり始めたら夢中になる。
それだけの話だ」
lines.label: s324
lines.maoEnglish:
“Everyone wants something. I had simply never found anything that could consume me.
The kind of fever in which you lose yourself―――tonight may have been my first.”
“Ha! Then when all is said and done, you’re a murderer too.”
“I don’t know. There still isn’t enough evidence to be certain. What about you? Is killing people enjoyable?”
“――――Are you stupid? If it were fun, I’d never stop doing it. There’s no reason behind this. Once I begin, I become absorbed. That’s all.”

lines.mirrorMoon:
"Everyone wants something, but I haven't found anything worth dreaming for.
A fire within me that caused me to lose my mind---tonight was maybe my first time feeling that."
"Hahaha.
That means you're a killer too."
"…… I don't know.
I can't be sure yet.
What about you, is killing fun?"
"----Are you stupid?
If it was fun, I'd be doing it non-stop.
There isn't any reason.
Once you start, you just get hooked."

lines.maoEnglish:
And yet here I was.
Akiha’s room lay at the far eastern end of the second floor, more than forty meters from mine. It was a place I would ordinarily have no reason to enter.

Now that I stopped to think, I was about to do something spectacularly improper.
“――Damn it, I’ve come this far—I’m not turning back now!”
Summoning my courage, I opened her door.

Someone like me had no right to be welcomed by Kohaku, Akiha, and Hisui.

　……秋葉も琥珀さんも気付かない、俺本人だって気付かないような、突然の眩暈に、翡翠は気がついてくれたみたいだ。
　だがそれで薄れていく意識が止まってくれるワケでもない。
　ばたん、と。
　糸の切れた人形のように、体が床に倒れこんだ。

Hisui called to me softly.
Neither Akiha nor Kohaku had noticed the sudden dizziness—apparently even I had not recognized it until it struck—yet Hisui had.
But her voice could do nothing to stop the darkness swallowing my mind.
My body struck the floor.
I fell like a puppet whose strings had been cut.

lines.maoEnglish:
“Ah―――――”
When I came to, I was lying in my own room.
I was in bed, and Akiha was sitting before me.
“Akiha?”
“Brother? You're awake?”
Akiha released a breath of relief.
“I see—I collapsed from anemia again.”
“Yes. You slept for almost seven hours, Brother.”
“―――I see. Perhaps all the sleep I've missed lately caught up with me. Sorry. I've caused you trouble again.”

「何を言うんですか。
兄さんの体が不安定なのは兄さんの責任ではないでしょう？
　兄さんは私の兄さんなんですから、看病をするのは当たり前です。
迷惑だというのでしたら、そう思われるほうがよっぽど迷惑です」
「……そっか。
それじゃお礼を言うのはやめとく。
兄妹なら当然のことだもんな、こんなの」
「なんだ、それだけ言えるんでしたらもう大丈夫みたいですね」
　言って、秋葉は俺の熱を計った。
　熱は三十七度六分。
平熱より一度ばかり高い程度。
lines.label: s414
lines.maoEnglish:
“What are you saying, Brother? Brother's poor health is hardly Brother's fault. Brother is my brother, so of course I will nurse you. If anything is troublesome, it is hearing you call yourself a burden.”
“All right. Then I won't thank you. This is only natural between siblings.”
“If you can say that much, you must be fine.”
Akiha took my temperature.
It was 37.6 degrees—barely a degree above normal.

“I'm still not quite myself.”
I drew a long breath.
Somehow my entire day off had vanished.
Still, if Hisui had spent the whole day beside me, perhaps it had not been wasted after all――――

lines.label: s414
lines.maoEnglish:
After breakfast, I went to the entrance hall.
Hisui had brought my bag ahead of me and was already waiting.
“I’ll come straight home today, so I should be back around four. And you don’t need to stand here waiting to greet me.”
“Understood. Please take care, Master Shiki.”
“Thanks. I’m off, Hisui.”
I waved to Hisui as she bowed deeply, then ran down the hill.
